clue.text: Withdraw and wander across border, not hard

indicators.note: one word lying across another spans it, so the wandering word straddles the border word
hard is abbreviated to a single letter, and 'not' tells us to drop that letter

blocks.note: to rove is to wander
a hem is the border of a garment

explanation.surface: A traveller retreats and drifts over a frontier, avoiding difficult terrain.
explanation.walkthrough: H for hard is the pencil-grade convention; the border word is trimmed before going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove something is to take it away or pull it out, the same as withdrawing it.

clue.text: Country club ripe for reform

indicators.note: something ready for reform is about to be reshaped, so these letters will be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A rural members' club is overdue for a shake-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country club' reads as one phrase, but 'Country' is the definition and 'club ripe' is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A republic is a state without a monarch, so it is one kind of nation.

clue.text: Mother quietly forming plan

blocks.note: Ma is an informal word for mother
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: A mum silently works out her scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A map can be a diagram or layout, and to map something out is to plan it, so a map serves as a plan.

clue.text: Government ending in ruin, engulfed by corruption and acrimony

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter, so only that letter of the next word is kept
whatever is engulfed is swallowed up inside something else, so these letters go within the outer word

blocks.note: first part of vice, which means corruption
rule is government
the last letter of ruin
rest of vice

explanation.surface: A regime collapses amid graft and bitter recriminations.
explanation.walkthrough: RULE plus the N of ruin sits inside VICE (corruption), giving VIRULENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Virulence is extreme bitterness or hostility in speech, which is what acrimony describes.

clue.text: Poor saint given the blame

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for saint
to be rapped is to be rebuked or blamed

explanation.surface: A penniless holy man is unfairly accused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' looks like pity for the saint, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Strapped, as in strapped for cash, describes someone short of money, which is being poor.

clue.text: Hard thing to say to new visitor involving mixture of wit and hesitation

indicators.note: a mixture jumbles its ingredients, so the letters of the word that follows are scrambled
to involve something is to take it in, so the visitor word wraps around the mixed letters

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
a guest is a visitor
the letters of wit rearranged
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A newcomer struggles to say something, stumbling between wit and hesitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' looks like a link after the definition, but it supplies letters. Only the three letters of wit are mixed, not the whole phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A tongue-twister is a phrase deliberately designed to be difficult to pronounce quickly.

clue.text: Embarrass sailor when joined by husband

blocks.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
as can mean when
h is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A seaman is put to shame when his husband turns up.
explanation.definitionFit: To abash someone is to make them feel ashamed or self-conscious, the same as embarrassing them.

clue.text: Student of stamps from Hawaii absorbed by illustration on catalogue

indicators.note: what is absorbed is soaked up inside something else, so the Hawaii letters go within the illustration word

blocks.note: a plate is a full-page illustration in a book
HI is the postal abbreviation for Hawaii
a catalogue is a list

explanation.surface: A stamp collector studies a Hawaiian picture in a dealer's catalogue.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed after, so the catalogue word comes last. A plate is a full-page picture in a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A philatelist collects and studies postage stamps, so is literally a student of them.

clue.text: Protest over central features of latest downgrade

indicators.note: the central features of a word are the letters at its middle, so only those are kept

blocks.note: a demo is a protest march
the middle two letters of latest

explanation.surface: A protest is staged over the newest cutbacks.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts DEMO above TE.
explanation.definitionFit: To demote someone is to move them to a lower rank, which is to downgrade them.

clue.text: Flimsy place in Australia with pest outside

indicators.note: the pest word stands outside the place, wrapping round it

blocks.note: first part of pain, a pest or nuisance
Perth is the capital of Western Australia
rest of pain

explanation.surface: An Australian town is plagued by insects, its buildings feeble.
explanation.walkthrough: A pain, as in 'a pain in the neck', is a pest; it wraps round PERTH to give PAPER-THIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something paper-thin is as thin as a sheet of paper, so weak and insubstantial.

clue.text: Allotted place held by one who's admired more than US president

indicators.note: what is held by something sits within its grasp, so the allotted place goes inside the admired one

blocks.note: first part of hero, someone admired
a berth is an assigned sleeping place or mooring
rest of hero
over means more than

explanation.surface: A man allotted a post is admired more than the president.
explanation.walkthrough: The admired one is a hero, split after its third letter to take the allotted place.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbert Hoover was the thirty-first President of the United States, from 1929 to 1933.

clue.text: Combine in retreat, filled with love, following a principle

indicators.note: a retreating army goes back the way it came, so the combine word is read backwards
something filled with another thing holds it inside
coming after, so these letters are placed behind the article

blocks.note: taken as written
to mix is to combine
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A combine harvester backs away, loaded up, guided by a rule.
explanation.walkthrough: MIX turned round is XIM; O goes inside, after A: AXIOM. 'Combine' looks like the farm machine.
explanation.definitionFit: An axiom is a statement accepted as self-evidently true, a basic rule or principle.

clue.text: Precious stone in course of robbery lost

indicators.note: something found in the course of other words lies within their run of letters

blocks.note: the letters run across the join of these two words

explanation.surface: A jewel goes missing during a heist.
explanation.definitionFit: Beryl is a mineral gemstone, varieties of which include emerald and aquamarine.

clue.text: Create problems getting back to other ground

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so these letters are broken up and remade

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone causes trouble by returning to a different pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like a noun for a playing field; it is the past tense of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: To rock the boat is an idiom meaning to disturb a stable situation and stir up trouble.

clue.text: Plaster in unfinished project

blocks.note: first meaning: a coarse plaster of lime and gravel for outside walls
second meaning: a rough first draft or outline of a plan

explanation.surface: Building work is left half done, plastered over.
explanation.definitionFit: Roughcast is both a pebbly render for exterior walls and a preliminary, crudely shaped draft of a scheme.

clue.text: Certain tin, once damaged, fixed

indicators.note: a damaged thing is knocked out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
something fixed is stable

explanation.surface: A tin can, once dented, has definitely been repaired.
explanation.definitionFit: Incontestable means beyond dispute, so something incontestable is certain.

clue.text: Inwardly, not half grabbed by courageous idea

indicators.note: not half of a word means only half of it survives, so the back half is lost
something grabbed is held tight inside another's grip

blocks.note: brave means courageous
taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A bold thought held halfway inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inwardly' looks like an insertion signal but is the word to be halved.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainwave is a sudden clever thought or inspiration, so it is an idea.

clue.text: Write about railway climbing above spot up in mountains

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the write word goes round the railway letters
climbing in a down clue means rising from bottom to top, so the railway letters are read upward
in a down clue one part placed above another simply comes first
up in a down clue tells us the spot word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: to pen is to write
Ry is an abbreviation for railway
to spot is to see

explanation.surface: A travel writer describes a mountain railway climbing to a viewpoint high up.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'climbing' and 'up' work in a down clue, where reading upward means reading backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pyrenees are a mountain range forming the border between France and Spain.

clue.text: Act heartily, in unreal style, embracing it

definitions.text: Act heartily, in unreal style, embracing it

indicators.note: done in an unreal style, the words are not presented as they are but artificially remade
to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so the rearranged letters wrap round the last word

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to a ham: perform with gusto and artifice, throwing yourself into it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the answer: acting heartily in an unreal way and embracing the role is theatricality.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatricality is an exaggerated, showy manner suited to the stage, which is what overacting heartily and artificially produces.

clue.text: Doctor's account about one work of decorative art

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the account word goes round the one

blocks.note: MO, medical officer, is a doctor; add the S
ac is the abbreviation for account
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A physician describes a single piece of ornamental art.
explanation.walkthrough: MO, medical officer, is the usual crossword doctor, and the apostrophe-S is kept as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A mosaic is a picture or pattern made from small pieces of tile or glass, a decorative artwork.

clue.text: Drive away into plain and go too far

indicators.note: the drive-away word goes into the plain word, landing inside it

blocks.note: first part of overt, meaning plain or open
to shoo is to drive away
rest of overt

explanation.surface: A motorist heads off across flat country and goes too far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive' and 'plain' suggest a car crossing open country; SHOO goes inside OVERT.
explanation.definitionFit: To overshoot is to pass beyond a target or stopping point, which is going too far.

clue.text: Jargon from south and north taken in by convict

indicators.note: what is taken in by something is absorbed within it

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for south
an old lag is a convict
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Prison talk spread from one end of the country to the other via a prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: S, then N inside LAG: SLANG. 'Lag', as in old lag, is British slang for a prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang is informal vocabulary peculiar to a group, much like jargon, the specialised talk of a trade.

clue.text: Fool soldiers in compound

blocks.note: a nit, short for nitwit, is a fool
RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers

explanation.surface: An idiot is among troops inside a military camp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound' looks like an army enclosure; it is the chemical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitre is potassium nitrate, a chemical compound used in gunpowder and fertiliser.

clue.text: Smell air for meat at regular intervals

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means picking every other one and skipping the rest

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters

explanation.surface: Someone sniffs the air for the scent of a roast at mealtimes.
explanation.definitionFit: An aroma is a pleasant, distinctive odour, so it is a smell.

clue.text: Articulate poetry about Indonesian island

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the poetry word goes round the island

blocks.note: first part of verse, meaning poetry
Bali is an island in Indonesia
rest of verse

explanation.surface: Verses are written about a tropical island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articulate' looks like an adjective for the poetry; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To verbalise is to express something in words, which is what articulating a thought means.

clue.text: Essential part of Arctic ecosystem

indicators.note: a part of the following words is taken, so the letters lie inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across the join of these two words

explanation.surface: A statement about what polar habitats depend on.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: frozen water underpins life at the North Pole.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea ice is the foundation of polar habitats, supporting algae, seals and polar bears alike.

clue.text: Group around judge filled with self-esteem

indicators.note: something filled with another thing holds it inside

blocks.note: ca, circa, means around
to try a case is to judge it
ego is self-esteem

explanation.surface: A band of people surround a pompous magistrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like a container signal, but here it is CA, the abbreviation for circa; EGO fills TRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A category is a class or set of things sharing characteristics, so it is a group.

clue.text: Resolution keeping experts going without a break

indicators.note: keeping something is holding it inside, so the resolution word goes round the experts
going without something means doing without it, so the single letter named is dropped

blocks.note: res is an abbreviation for resolution
aces are experts

explanation.surface: A decision keeps the professionals working non-stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without a break' reads as one phrase meaning non-stop, but it splits: the A is dropped and 'break' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A recess is a pause in proceedings, such as a parliamentary holiday or a school playtime, so it is a break.
